name: Breakeven & unit economics
summary: Breakeven volume = Fixed costs ÷ (Price − Variable cost per unit). Payback = Investment ÷ annual profit. Use it to test whether a decision pays off and how many units or years it takes.
opening_line: The quickest test is breakeven: fixed costs divided by contribution margin per unit, compared with the volume we can realistically sell.
when_to_use: Any launch, investment or pricing decision with fixed costs
Checking whether a target is achievable (payback within N years)
when_not_to_use: As the whole structure. It's a tool inside market entry, pricing or investment frameworks

buckets.name: Inputs
questions: Price, variable cost, fixed costs, upfront investment?

buckets.name: Test
questions: Is the breakeven volume realistic vs market size and share?

industry_adaptations.note: Covers per day needed = fixed costs ÷ (average check − food & variable labour per cover).

common_mistakes: Mixing up per-unit and total costs
Forgetting time (no discounting) for long paybacks
Not comparing the breakeven with what's achievable
